Article.ArticleTitle: Aerobic exercise and blood pressure: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.

Abstract.AbstractText: Elevated blood pressure is a leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, and structured exercise programs are commonly recommended as a first-line intervention.
We pooled data from randomized controlled trials comparing supervised aerobic exercise against usual care, measuring change in systolic and diastolic blood pressure.

Aerobic exercise programs were associated with a mean reduction in systolic blood pressure of several millimeters of mercury, with more pronounced effects in participants who began with higher baseline readings.

Article.ArticleTitle: Sleep duration and metabolic markers: a systematic review.

Abstract.AbstractText: To systematically review studies relating habitual sleep duration to fasting glucose, insulin sensitivity, and lipid profiles in adults.

Short sleep duration, generally under six hours per night, was consistently associated with worse markers of glucose regulation across the reviewed studies, while long sleep duration showed more inconsistent associations.
